triage.root_cause: The native managed-worktree validation fixture omitted the now-required structured impact evidence and conflated source-alias ownership with an independent workspace contender.
The test treated a compact review-snapshot receipt as the persisted complete snapshot instead of resolving the current state record.
The packaged Hook test parsed an obsolete line-oriented interpreter field even though the packaged output was a structured checkpoint.
Two task-id subcases reused a source repository already held by an active task, so the exclusive repository claim correctly rejected the fixture before task-id validation.
The workspace contention fixture tried to create two active tasks over one exclusively claimed source and assumed branch names were globally exclusive across independent Git common directories.
The rollback test invoked schema-v2 cancellation without first previewing and confirming its exact transition intent.
The test root retained the macOS /var alias while the controller returned the canonical /private/var path.
The fixture removed additive index fields from a schema-v2 task but asserted that the unchanged stored task had become schema-v1.
The concurrent cancellation fixture omitted the required schema-v2 preview and shared confirmed intent, so both processes were rejected before exercising revision contention.
The test compared a current schema-v2 task against the legacy SCHEMA_VERSION alias instead of the task schema contract and the task's original version.

triage_policy: Every record is a test or validation-fixture defect exposed by existing production contracts. No failing behavior is accepted as a compatibility golden.
